equation_request.abstract: We present several families of graphs that allow both efficient quantum walk implementations and efficient quantum walk based search algorithms. For these graphs, we construct quantum circuits that explicitly implement the full quantum walk search algorithm, without reference to a ‘black box’ oracle. These circuits provide a practically implementable method to explore quantum walk based search algorithms with the aim of eventual real-world applications. We also provide a numerical analysis of a quantum walk based search along a twisted toroid family of graphs, which requires O($\sqrt{n}$ log($n$)) elementary 2-qubit quantum gate operations to find a marked node.

specification.problem: Coined discrete-time quantum walk search for a single known marked node on a degree-4 twisted-toroid graph with n=2^(2m) nodes, implemented as an explicit circuit with the marking compiled in (no black box).
specification.reconstruction_scope: One tiny instance, m=1 or m=2 (n=4 or 16), with Grover coin, flip-flop shift, a twist on x-wraparound, a compiled marked node, and a numerically chosen iteration count T. Statevector simulation, then position-register readout. Excludes the other graph families in the abstract, the exact twist definition from the paper, the O(sqrt(n) log n) gate-count proof, and large-n numerics.

symbols.meaning: lattice coordinates (little-endian, x in the low m bits, y in the high m bits)
twist offset applied to y when x wraps

equations.label: Initial state
equations.description: Uniform superposition over coin and position, made by Hadamards.
equations.justification: The sketch specifies Hadamards on the position and coin registers. The abstract does not state this.

equations.label: Marking and coin
equations.description: Phase flip on the marked position, compiled as a multi-controlled Z (X gates on the zero bits of w), followed by the Grover coin on the 2 coin qubits.
equations.justification: The sketch gives a coin phase flip at a fixed marked address and a Grover coin. The sign conventions are a choice. A full-coin flip is used here, and the sketch's phrase 'flipping the coin phase' is ambiguous.
assumptions: Marked-node phase applies to all coin values

equations.label: Twisted shift
equations.description: Flip-flop shift: move in the direction c and reverse the coin. Modular increments or decrements come from MCX cascades. When x wraps (x=2^m-1 going +x, or x=0 going -x), y also shifts by s, with the sign following the direction.
equations.justification: The sketch describes a conditional increment of the other coordinate on wraparound. The exact twist in the paper is unknown, so this is one plausible choice.

equations.label: Search evolution and success probability
equations.description: T iterations, where T maximizes P(T) in a numerical scan over T for small instances.
equations.abstract_quote: We also provide a numerical analysis of a quantum walk based search along a twisted toroid family of graphs
equations.justification: A numerical analysis implies scanning the marked-node probability. The sketch's T~sqrt(n) with a 1/log n peak is not stated in the abstract.
assumptions: the optimal T is found by classical simulation of the same circuit

equations.label: Gate scaling claim
equations.description: Claimed total two-qubit gate count for finding a marked node.
equations.abstract_quote: requires O($\sqrt{n}$ log($n$)) elementary 2-qubit quantum gate operations to find a marked node
equations.justification: Stated directly in the abstract. It is a claim, not a derivation, and is used here as a target only.

registers.name: pos
registers.role: x in the low m bits, y in the high m bits

registers.name: anc
registers.role: ancilla for multi-controlled gates, returned to |0>

specification.initial_state: All qubits |0>, then H on coin and pos, giving the uniform state; the ancilla stays |0>.

steps.description: Prepare the uniform superposition with Hadamards.
Repeat T times: apply the marking phase flip at w, then the Grover coin.
Apply the coin-controlled twisted shift, with wrap detection and the y increment.
Choose T by simulating and maximizing P(T). Read out the position register.

specification.measurement: Measure the 2m position qubits only. Qiskit little-endian: the last character of the counts key is bit 0, which is x bit 0. Do not measure the coin or the ancilla.
specification.classical_postprocessing: Take the most frequent position outcome as the marked node, and decode x = low m bits and y = high m bits.
assumptions: Choose m=1 or 2 as the instance
Coin-based walk with Grover coin and flip-flop shift
Single known marked node compiled in, no black-box queries
Twist is y+1 when x wraps (a guess)
Success probability may be only about 1/log n and is boosted by repetition
missing_information: Exact twisted-toroid graph definition (twist size and direction)
Paper's exact oracle and coin conventions

Other graph families in the abstract
